'''William James O'Reilly Jr.''' (born September 10, 1949) is an American television host, author, and conservative political commentator. He gained prominence as the host of ''The O'Reilly Factor'', which aired on the [[Fox News Channel]] from 1996 to 2017. Throughout his career, O'Reilly has been involved in various controversies and has occasionally promoted or entertained conspiracy theories, drawing criticism from different quarters.

== Controversies ==
O'Reilly's tenure at Fox News was marked by several high-profile controversies. He faced numerous allegations of sexual harassment, which he and the network settled out of court, leading to his departure from Fox News in 2017.

In terms of on-air content, O'Reilly has faced criticism for comments considered by some to be racially insensitive or inflammatory. His reporting and commentary at times have skirted into the realm of conspiracy theories, particularly with regard to his treatment of certain political or social issues.

== Conspiracy Theories ==
O'Reilly has been accused of entertaining or promoting conspiracy theories, particularly during his time on ''The O'Reilly Factor''. This includes casting doubt on the veracity of mainstream accounts on issues like gun control and government action. His approach has often drawn parallels to more overt purveyors of conspiracy theories.

== Connections to Alex Jones ==
While there is no direct collaboration or partnership between Bill O'Reilly and [[Alex Jones]], the controversial right-wing media personality known for his conspiracy theory-driven program ''Infowars'', both have been part of broader discussions related to conservative media and the dissemination of controversial or unverified claims. Some critics have mentioned O'Reilly in the context of Jones and others in their commentary on the impact of sensationalist or conspiratorial narratives in media. However, O'Reilly has not publicly aligned himself with Jones, maintaining a distinct approach to his commentary and broadcasting.

== Bibliography ==
O'Reilly is also a prolific author, having written numerous books, many of which have been bestsellers, including his "Killing" series, which covers historical events with a dramatic flair.
